title: Bobble Hero! [iOS Beta] in TestFlight
author: renge-refurion
selftext:
I've been making a cozy puzzle game for iPhone and I'm at the point where my friends and family are too nice to me about it so I decided to ask strangers on the internet lol.

It's called Bobble Hero. You know those capsule toy machines? Each level is one of those. You tap capsules to fill orders, and when you clear the machine a little toy person who was stuck inside gets out and moves back into their town. Then you rebuild the town for them. There’s 400+ levels and 8 full towns built so far.

Built primarily using my own dev and app experience, assets using tripo and claude opus/fable as needed to tighten things and bug hunt/QA for me in the simulator (godsend for release testing IMO). I've released apps before but review times are insane now so getting things right the first time is essential. Best tip I can give is to have Opus cross reference the metadata and binary of your app against the current (essential) guidelines and make a walkthrough video for the reviewers (NOT a teaser/marketing video).

There's a story running through it about who sealed everybody in, plus a dice trail, a peg drop game, a claw game and toys to collect.

It's free, not for sale yet but will be once I get enough feedback and dial the difficulty in. Tuning the puzzles has been tricky which is why I need more players.

Purchases don't charge anything in TestFlight, so tap whatever you like. English and Spanish versions available. Special kudos to my spanish testers!

You can reply here, or take a screenshot in the game and send it through TestFlight, which goes straight to me. Blunt is good! 

[https://testflight.apple.com/join/35qG6rXc](https://testflight.apple.com/join/35qG6rXc)

There are 200 spots. Thanks to anyone who gives it ten minutes.

comments.author: SillyHamm
comments.body: I love the idea, but it too easy? I don’t played too much but I didn’t see any challenge. The rewards are very well done tho

replies.author: renge-refurion
replies.body: This is super helpful thanks. Difficulty tuning has been a moving target for me. Will get to work on improving
